stories.headline: Westport’s Compo Beach dog rules return Oct. 1 through March 2027
stories.summary: Seasonal dog rules at Westport’s Compo Beach take effect Thursday, Oct. 1, and run through March 31, 2027, Patch reported. Dogs are barred from the pavilion, playground, and walkways; they must be leashed everywhere except the posted off-leash beach south of the pavilion, including South Beach. Owners must pick up waste, violations carry a $77 fine, and animals remain banned from Westport athletic fields and playgrounds year-round, including all of Luciano Park.

stories.headline: Stamford speed cameras go live in October at 14 school-zone spots
stories.summary: Stamford’s automated speed cameras will become operational in October at 14 locations across seven school zones, Mayor Caroline Simmons announced, Patch reported Sept. 30. An exact start date is still pending. Tickets apply when drivers exceed the posted limit by 11 mph or more; a 45-day warning period comes first, then $50 for a first offense and $75 for later ones, with no license points or insurance hits. Camera streets cover Cloonan, Dolan, Springdale, Toquam, Stamford High, Julia A. Stark, K.T. Murphy, and Strawberry Hill school areas.

stories.headline: Trump and Vance open midterm blitz in deep-red Texas, Oklahoma, and Florida
stories.summary: President Trump’s Thursday Texas and Oklahoma stops kick off a self-described 32-day midterm blitz through Nov. 3, while Vice President JD Vance stumps in Florida, the Associated Press reported via WTOP. Trump tours a Denton truck plant tied to Sen. hopeful Ken Paxton’s race, then rallies in Durant for Oklahoma gubernatorial nominee Mike Mazzei; aides say red-state stops also hit Dallas–Fort Worth and Florida panhandle media markets. Trump blamed messaging—“We’re not getting the word out”—as Republicans worry about costs, gas prices, and the Iran war.

stories.headline: DHS: Fairfax released Honduran child-sex suspect despite ICE detainer; ICE rearrests him
stories.summary: ICE rearrested Honduran national Oscar Evaristo Nunez on Sept. 15 after Fairfax County, Virginia, released him despite an ICE detainer, DHS said, Fox News reported Sept. 30. Nunez had been arrested Aug. 27, 2025, on aggravated sexual battery involving children and nonconsensual filming of a minor; DHS said he illegally entered near Arizona around 2003 and remains in ICE custody. Secretary Markwayne Mullin blasted “sanctuary politicians,” while Fairfax did not immediately comment and Gov. Abigail Spanberger has rolled back some state ICE 287(g) cooperation since January.

stories.headline: White House drops CNN from TV press pool for Trump’s Texas–Oklahoma trip
stories.summary: The White House removed CNN from Thursday’s television press-pool duty for President Trump’s Denton, Texas, and Durant, Oklahoma, trip even though Sunday’s rotation had listed the network, Mediaite reported Oct. 1. The switch comes days after a federal judge temporarily restored White House-grounds access for CNN, MS NOW, and Politico, without expressly covering Air Force One or travel-pool slots. CNN was similarly blocked from a Tennessee AF1 pool last weekend; counsel Theodore Boutrous again called the broader ban a First Amendment and due-process violation.

stories.headline: Penguins steamroll Flyers 7–0 in season opener; Silovs earns shutout
stories.summary: Nicholas Robertson scored twice in his Penguins debut and Arturs Silovs stopped 19 shots as Pittsburgh blanked Philadelphia 7–0 in both clubs’ opener Wednesday at Xfinity Mobile Arena, NHL.com reported Oct. 1. Filip Hallander had a goal and two assists; Hendrix Lapierre, Ville Koivunen, Evgeni Malkin, and Egor Chinakhov also scored, with Malkin reaching 100 career points against the Flyers. Sidney Crosby called it the “right mentality” on the road; the win tied Pittsburgh’s biggest shutout of Philadelphia and lifted Crosby–Malkin–Letang to a record 494 regular-season wins together.

stories.headline: Jets–Bears Week 4: Hall, Mitchell, Taylor, Parham doubtful; Fitzpatrick questionable
stories.summary: Ahead of Sunday’s 1 p.m. ET FOX game at Soldier Field, NBC Sports lists Jets RB Breece Hall (thigh), WR Adonai Mitchell (finger), TE Mason Taylor (thumb), and LG Dylan Parham as doubtful, with S Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin) and LB Kiko Mauigoa (quad) questionable. Chicago’s Caleb Williams (hamstring) is also doubtful, pushing Tyson Bagent into the likely start after Case Keenum’s win over Philadelphia. Geno Smith has opened 783 yards, 4 TDs, and 0 INTs; markets have the Bears around −3.5 / −175 with a total near 42.5.

stories.headline: Apple Mail on Mac may stop syncing Microsoft 365 as Exchange EWS goes dark
stories.summary: Microsoft began disabling Exchange Web Services by default in Exchange Online on Oct. 1, cutting the protocol Apple Mail and Calendar on Mac still use for many Microsoft 365 work accounts, MacRumors reported. Organizations that keep EWS enabled are unaffected for now; Microsoft plans a permanent EWS shutdown April 1, 2027. Apple says it is working with Microsoft on Graph API support in a future macOS 27 update that has not shipped yet. iPhone and iPad keep working via Exchange ActiveSync; IT can re-enable EWS or move Mac users to Outlook.

stories.headline: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 set for 11:10 a.m. ET liftoff to the space station
stories.summary: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13—astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA’s Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov—is targeting an 11:10 a.m. ET Falcon 9 / Dragon launch from Cape Canaveral SLC-40 on Oct. 1, NASA’s commercial crew blog said. Weather was only about 40% favorable at the pad (cumulus, thick layers, precipitation). The crew will join Expedition 75 for roughly six months of research spanning stem-cell tissues, crop production, and medical diagnostics as Commercial Crew keeps private U.S. rides to the ISS running.

stories.headline: SpaceX Transporter-18 lofting Google’s Project Suncatcher AI satellite today
stories.summary: SpaceX’s Transporter-18 rideshare is scheduled for Oct. 1 from Vandenberg during a window opening at 2:18 p.m. ET, carrying 130 payloads including Google’s Project Suncatcher pathfinder to test TPUs in orbit for radiation and thermal performance, Space.com reported. Cowboy Space’s Reason-1 power-beaming demo and Starfish Space’s first Otter servicing satellite also fly. The Falcon 9 booster targets a Vandenberg landing on its 25th flight; SpaceX also planned Crew-13 and an NROL-97 Falcon Heavy the same day.

stories.headline: Insta360 eyes smart glasses and two mirrorless cameras beyond 360 gear
stories.summary: Insta360 cofounder Max Richter told The Verge the company is experimentally building smart glasses aimed at convenient high-quality capture rather than an on-face AI assistant, Photography Talk summarized Sept. 30. Founder JK Liu previously confirmed two mirrorless cameras in development—one with an unusual shape—and floated a possible CP+ 2027 prototype. Insta360 holds about 73% of worldwide 360-camera shipments and has opened a Times Square flagship, while stressing it is distancing from drone brand Antigravity amid U.S. ban risk; no glasses or mirrorless names, prices, or ship dates are announced.

stories.headline: Canon RF 90mm f/2.8 IS STM Macro reportedly next—budget 1:1 alternative to the L
stories.summary: Canon Rumors points to an upcoming RF 90mm f/2.8 IS STM Macro as a non-L, mid-tier 1:1 option versus the ~$1,300 RF 100mm f/2.8L Macro, The Phoblographer reported Sept. 25. Patent-linked designs suggest a compact ~100 mm length with moving middle groups for life-size magnification, aimed at hobbyists and APS-C shooters (~144 mm equivalent). No price or date is official; some fans still want a longer RF 180mm macro instead of another mid-tele STM.

stories.headline: Idaho Renaissance Faire’s ‘Festival of Fools’ returns to Meridian Oct. 10–11
stories.summary: The nonprofit Idaho Renaissance Faire returns to 6054 W. Cherry Lane in Meridian Oct. 10–11 from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. with an Italian Renaissance “Festival of Fools” theme, Idaho News 6 reported Sept. 25. Organizers promise live performers, vendors, characters, and the expected turkey legs while raising money for local arts and theater programs. Costumes are welcome but not required; tickets and details are on the faire’s website.

stories.headline: Five Finger Death Punch marks 20 years in Austin with Cody Jinks and Eva Under Fire
stories.summary: Five Finger Death Punch’s 20th-anniversary stop at Germania Insurance Amphitheater in Austin on Monday mixed new Legacy material with catalog staples, Maxazine’s live review said Sept. 30. Eva Under Fire opened and Cody Jinks mid-billed before FFDP opened with “Welcome to the Circus,” stacked “Eye of the Storm” and “Legacy,” and closed with “The Bleeding.” Moody quipped they’d tour with anyone “who isn’t going to have Beyoncé on their next record” as the North American leg continues into late October.

stories.headline: Blue Ridge Parkway fall drive: elevation timing, Mabry Mill, and Linn Cove tips
stories.summary: TourMe’s 2026 Blue Ridge Parkway guide notes the free 469-mile ridge road from Shenandoah to the Smokies sees two to three million October drivers, with color peaking first above 5,000 feet in late September and mid-elevations around Oct. 8–15. Practical tips cover 45 mph pacing, sunrise fog at Craggy Gardens and Waterrock Knob, Mabry Mill’s living-history millpond photos (peak ~Oct. 15–22), and the Linn Cove Viaduct’s top-down engineering story. Detours to Floyd, Blowing Rock, and Asheville round out a leaf-peeping plan beyond overlook selfies.

stories.headline: LEGO October wave now live worldwide—Astro Bot GWP and Star Wars 2× points
stories.summary: Jay’s Brick Blog confirmed Oct. 1 that LEGO’s October wave is live worldwide, including Holiday House, Bookshop: Book Nook, Wallace & Gromit, Downton Abbey, PlayStation, UCS Executor, Pokémon Poké Ball, Wednesday, and Avengers: Doomsday sets. Shoppers spending over $150 through Oct. 7 can claim the Astro Bot gift-with-purchase while stocks last; Executor buyers get Darth Vader’s Lightsaber GWP through Oct. 10, and selected Star Wars sets (not Executor) earn 2× Insiders points. Popular early picks flagged include Wallace & Gromit, PlayStation, Holiday House, and Doomsday Epic Battle.
